About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Businesses need a clear, reliable way to work with their vendors, from collecting information during onboarding to keeping vendor records accurate as they purchase and pay. Vendors need a straightforward way to provide details and stay connected with the businesses they serve. Ramp’s Vendor Management & Portal team builds the systems behind those experiences.

We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to make vendor information easier to collect, connect, and use across Ramp. You’ll work on services that support vendor profiles, onboarding requests, and the vendor portal, where identity, permissions, and data accuracy matter. You’ll own meaningful projects from design through launch and partner with product, design, and other engineering teams to make these workflows dependable for both businesses and vendors.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and build backend services and APIs for vendor profiles, onboarding, and portal workflows.

  • Improve how vendor records and portal accounts are matched and connected, reducing duplicate work and making shared information more reliable.

  • Build workflows for collecting and updating vendor information, including payment and tax details, with clear permissions and accurate data handling.

  • Make vendor data available consistently across the products that depend on it, including procurement and bill pay.

  • Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration.

  • Raise the quality of the team’s systems through thoughtful design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship.

What You’ll Need

  • Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows.

  • Strong judgment about data integrity, access controls, reliability, and the tradeoffs involved in evolving existing systems.

  • A track record of independently leading complex engineering projects from design to production.

  • Product sense and curiosity about how businesses and vendors actually use the workflows you build.

  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach to working across engineering, product, and design.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with vendor management, procurement, accounts payable, or other business finance workflows.

  • Experience with identity matching, deduplication, or sharing data safely across accounts and products.

  • Experience improving operational visibility and reliability in systems that handle sensitive business information.

What is Kalshi?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to help Kalshi’s Growth team move faster. You’ll build tools, automate workflows, ship experiments, and solve the technical problems that stand between an idea and a launch.

You’ll work directly with growth and marketing to turn loosely defined requests into working software. Some days you’ll build something new. Other days you’ll debug an integration, fix a broken workflow, or ship a small improvement that saves the team hours. You’ll own the details and follow through until the work is live and working.

This is an opportunity for an exceptional and fast-moving early-career engineer who loves building and learns quickly. We’re scaling fast, and your scope will grow as you demonstrate what you can own.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Build and maintain tools, integrations, and automations that help the Growth team execute faster.

  • Turn growth and marketing ideas into working prototypes, experiments, and production tools.

  • Troubleshoot broken workflows and integrations, resolve urgent issues, and address recurring problems at the source.

  • Connect APIs and data sources to reduce manual work and make existing tools work better together.

  • Use AI coding tools to accelerate development while taking responsibility for code quality, testing, and reliability.

  • Work directly with teammates to clarify requests, prioritize competing needs, and communicate progress.

  • Translate spontaneous business needs into verifiable technical solutions, with a short turnaround time.

  • Own projects from initial request through launch, monitoring, and iteration.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Must have a Bachelor’s Degree (or foreign equivalent) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a closely related field, plus 2 years of experience working on production systems.

  • Strong coding fundamentals and evidence that you can build and ship working software. Demonstrated ability developing, testing, and maintaining production software. Used languages like Python, Go (Golang), JavaScript to write polished production code. Some mobile development experience with Flutter is a plus.

  • Demonstrated ability working with both relational and NoSQL database systems, such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB, including schema design, query optimization, and data modeling.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of APIs, databases, version control.

  • Ability to learn new tools, frameworks, and processes quickly and in a hands-on, feet-first fashion.

  • Resourcefulness in problem-solving – knowing when/how to ask questions while primarily acting independently.

  • Hands-on experience using AI coding tools, with the judgment to understand, debug, and improve what they produce. Your ability to multitask here is important.

  • Resourcefulness when requirements are incomplete. You ask good questions, find a practical path forward, and keep moving.

  • Strong follow-through and attention to detail. You care whether the thing you shipped actually works.

  • Comfort managing several requests at once and adapting when priorities change.

  • Readiness to put out daily fires and respond to frequent changing requests.

  • Curiosity about how software can help a business reach more users and grow.

  • Clear communication and the ability to work independently while asking for help when needed.

New graduates and engineers in the first few years of their careers are encouraged to apply. We care about what you’ve built, how you think, and how quickly you learn.

Bonus Points:

  • You’ve built and launched a product, side project, or business that people actually use.

  • Experience with marketing technology, analytics, tracking, or experimentation tools.

  • Experience running online advertisements, dropshipping, sneaker botting, restaurant reservations, video game servers, etc. You have a knack for niche applications of software and care a lot about shipping fast at scale.

  • Experience building web applications, internal tools, or workflow automations.

  • Interest in prediction markets, finance, or consumer technology.

NYC PAY TRANSPARENCY DISCLOSURE

Salary Range: 115,000 and up annually, plus equity and benefits.

Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and broad variance in experience levels within each title. If your compensation expectations exceed this range, we encourage you to reach out. We’re always happy to discuss.

Our Culture

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. We are committed to our vision of building something big… but also useful: a product that brings more truth through the power of markets.

Kalshians are Kalshi’s most important asset: we pick Kalshians carefully, so we trust them fully on day 1.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

Kalshi is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our mission and values, we’d love to hear from you.

Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

We're seeking a Senior Business Architect (Canada) for ACCC: someone who can go deep on brokerage operations across accounts, trading, clearing, settlement, custody, and asset servicing, and can turn that operating knowledge into clear requirements and turn that into clear requirements Product and Engineering can build.

You are the bridge between how the Canadian brokerage actually works and the product roadmap. You lead structured discovery with counterparts and work out how partner firms, account opening, clearing, custody, and day-to-day operations fit together, then write that down as epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and open decisions.

Success is measured by: requirements and designs teams can build without guessing; a clear split between what the system does and what people still do at launch; solution options that Product and Engineering can sequence; and a backlog tied to ACCC milestones and capabilities.

What You'll Walk Into

You won't be starting from zero. You'll be owning live problems:

  • Operations scope: defining what ACCC must support across accounts, trading, clearing, settlement, custody, books and records, and asset servicing.
  • Partner firm handoffs: what partners send us, what we send back, and who does what across accounts, trades, cash, and securities.
  • Account and trade lifecycle: account opening, settlement in Canada through CDS, failed trades, transfers, and corporate actions such as dividends and splits.
  • Platform gap analysis: comparing today's Alpaca platform with Canadian brokerage operations requirements to decide what we reuse, change, or build.
  • Launch scope: separating what must work on day one from what follows, including registered accounts (TFSA, RRSP, RESP), more products, and more partner services.
  • Open decisions: logging each one with an owner so it gets closed or consciously deferred.

What you’ll own

Requirements across ACCC’s brokerage operations, and what comes next:

  • Map brokerage operations end to end across these areas: broker onboarding, account carrying, trade clearing/settlement, custody of cash/securities, books & records, financing (if in scope), corporate actions, transfers, exceptions, and reporting
  • Help define target operating models and capability designs: what the platform must do, what stays manual (for now), what is control vs. feature, what is Canada-specific vs. reusable globally
  • Turn regulatory and operational obligations into product requirements: what the platform must do, what stays manual (for now), what is control vs. feature, what is Canada-specific vs. reusable globally
  • Write epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and edge cases that Product and Engineering can build against.
  • Produce the artifacts teams actually use: process maps, capability matrices, requirement specs, data/field definitions, state machines, exception catalogs, RACI for build vs. run, and decision logs
  • Work with Product Managers and Engineering to sequence MVP → launch → scale: must-haves for go-live vs. post-launch backlog across these operating areas (e.g. additional account types, asset classes, IB services, automation)
  • Interface across Product, Engineering, Ops, and Compliance: translate business need into buildable scope; escalate open decisions with clear owners and options
  • Run structured discovery: workshops, SME interviews, gap analysis vs. current Alpaca platform, peer operating models where useful
  • Keep requirements automation- and AI-aware: flag where STP, rules, and AI-assisted exception handling should be designed in—not bolted on later
  • Flag where straight-through processing, rules, and AI-assisted exception handling should be designed from the start.
  • Maintain a living requirements backlog tied to ACCC milestones, risks, and open decisions

Who you are (Must-Haves)

  • Excited about what Alpaca is building and about standing up Canadian brokerage operations.
  • Comfortable operating as a senior IC reporting to the President — driving clarity across Product, Engineering, Ops, and Compliance without needing a formal team.
  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, or equivalent.
  • 8+ years as a business architect, business analyst, consultant or in product operations within brokerage, clearing, custody, or capital markets.
  • Comfortable translating brokerage operating processes and regulatory requirements into product language (you don’t need to be a lawyer or CCO)
  • Strong structured analysis: flows, entities, states, exceptions, controls, and what breaks if a step is missing.
  • Clear writing: specs, diagrams, and decisions others can execute against.
  • Collaborative with Ops SMEs, PMs, Engineering, and Compliance; curious enough to dig; disciplined enough to close loops
  • Bias to precision over vague “requirements fluff”; you know when something is a product change vs. an ops procedure vs. a policy decision
  • Judgment to tell a product change from an operating procedure or a policy decision.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills across operations, product, engineering, and compliance.

Who you might be (Nice-to-Haves)

  • Experience on a carrying, self-clearing, or custody build.
  • Canadian dealer, carrying broker, or introducing broker experience.
  • Prior business architecture or enterprise/solution architecture exposure in capital markets
  • Familiarity with CDS or Canadian settlement workflows.
  • Experience with registered accounts or Canadian tax requirements (TFSA, RRSP, RESP).
  • Background with API or platform brokerage products.
  • Experience working at a fintech, startup, or greenfield launch.
  • AI-native workflow: recurring use of tools like Cursor, Claude, or ChatGPT in spec drafting, discovery synthesis, and gap analysis.
  • Experience shaping greenfield capability roadmaps with executive sponsors

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

Prime's research compounds when other researchers can run it, inspect it, extend it, and build on it. Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Prime's public surface already includes verifiers v1, prime-rl's extensible algorithms layer, and more than 2,500 community environments.
